tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDITED 2026-07-26 (deep QA pass). El Faro (lighthouse) at western tip of Isla Canales de Afuera. CORRECTION: coiba-island.com removed from validation_source — fresh fetch of coiba-island.com's dive site page confirms it does NOT mention Faro/El Faro or bull/oceanic blacktip sharks anywhere; the earlier citation was unsupported. Replaced with scubaboard.com (thread 330598, 'Diving report about Coiba Island, Panama', 2010) which explicitly lists 'El Faro del Canales' among sites dived and independently corroborates the encrusting-sponge/orange-cup-coral/finger-sponge/gorgonian substrate description found in other independent write-ups of the same site cluster. Three independently re-verified domains: panamadivecenter.com, divemasteraustin.com, scubaboard.com. Depth: panamadivecenter.com states reef descends to ~30m; divemasteraustin.com's single-visit log recorded 64ft/19m max — retained 30m as the operator-published maximum, noted as a range. Bull sharks and oceanic blacktips confirmed by both panamadivecenter.com and divemasteraustin.com independently. Manta rays and whale sharks (seasonal, Dec-Apr) confirmed by panamadivecenter.com. Garden eels confirmed by divemasteraustin.com. No factual claims required removal this pass.

UNRESOLVED. Re-checked again 2026-07-26 (deep QA pass): fresh WebSearch for "Machete Point" Coiba dive site Panama still returns no operator, PADI, ScubaBoard, or database listing under this name. One tangential search hit referenced a Coiba site nicknamed after a former Coiba prison inmate turned park ranger, entered at 13m depth — but no name or coordinates tie that anecdote to "Machete Point," so it was not used to confirm this entry. 'Machete Caves' remains a distinct Bocas del Toro (Caribbean coast) location, not Coiba. Validated=false retained. Do not publish until confirmed by a local operator.

RE-AUDITED 2026-07-26 (deep QA pass). CORRECTION/REMOVAL: the '5,000 years old' reef age claim was re-checked against a fresh fetch of coibanationalpark.com's Bahia Damas page and is NOT present on the page in its current form (page states only the 135-hectare/335-acre size and 'one of the largest reefs in Central America'). No other source confirms a reef age. This claim has been REMOVED as unverifiable — a hallucination-removal per the anti-hallucination policy. UPGRADE: the 'second-largest coral reef in the Eastern Pacific' claim, previously flagged as single-source, is now independently confirmed by THREE sources on fresh re-fetch: coibanationalpark.com ('one of the largest reefs in Central America... second largest coral reef in the Eastern Pacific'), tourismpanama.com ('135 hectares, one of the most extensive marine habitats on the continent'), and thearkdivers.com ('THE BAHIA DAMAS REEF IN COIBA IS THE SECOND-LARGEST CORAL REEF IN THE EASTERN PACIFIC OCEAN'). Caveat retained and strengthened: the park-wide '800 fish species / 33 shark species' figures are NOT Bahia Damas-specific — added ocean.si.edu (Smithsonian Ocean Portal) as a fourth source, which independently states Coiba National Park hosts 'nearly 800 species of fish, including 33 species of sharks, and 20 species of cetaceans' park-wide (matches thearkdivers.com's '33 different shark species' figure). These remain explicitly labeled park-wide, not site-specific, in the markdown.

RE-AUDITED 2026-07-26 (deep QA pass) — MAJOR CORRECTION. Fresh fetch of the PADI dive site page's actual 'Common Sightings' tag list shows only FOUR species/categories: Sharks, Whales, Dolphins, Turtles — not the 17-species list previously carried in validation_source/markdown (hammerhead sharks, barracuda, batfish, eagle rays, eels, flounders, groupers, lobsters, manta rays, moray eels, parrotfish, pipefish, porcupinefish, pufferfish, reef sharks, stingrays, yellowtail snapper). That expanded list was NOT found on the current PADI page and has been REMOVED as unconfirmed — a significant hallucination-removal. Also removed: the specific attribution of 'hammerhead sharks' to this site — hammerhead activity in Coiba is documented at the Contreras Islands (thearkdivers.com, scubacoiba.com, panamadivecenter.com), not at Jicarón/Jicarita; no source ties hammerheads specifically to Jicarita. coiba-island.com and panamadivecenter.com were removed from validation_source (neither page mentions Jicarita/Jicarón by name with site-specific detail). Two new genuine sources found and substituted: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jicarita (dedicated article — confirms geography, and that surrounding waters host 'rays, sharks, sailfish, marlin, yellowfin tuna, dolphins, whales, and orcas') and coibanationalpark.com/jicaron.html (independently corroborates the same species set: rays, sharks, sailfish, marlin, dolphins, whales, orcas, yellowfin tuna). Depth: no source gives a numeric depth for Jicarita specifically; retained 30m as an unconfirmed working estimate consistent with regional advanced drop-off sites — flagged as such in markdown rather than presented as a sourced fact.

RE-AUDITED 2026-07-26 (deep QA pass) — SOURCE COUNT SHORTFALL, FLAGGED PER DEEP-QA POLICY. On this pass, panamadivecenter.com's and coiba-island.com's full site listings were re-fetched in their entirety and neither one mentions 'Santa Cruz' anywhere; the previous validation_source citing all three was overstated. All specific claims (32ft/10m avg, 66ft/20m max, mated scorpionfish pair, 'aquarium-like' hard coral, strong current in the shallows) were reconfirmed against a fresh fetch of divemasteraustin.com and are accurate to that source.

RE-AUDITED 2026-07-26 (deep QA pass) — CORRECTIONS. Coordinates and 14-42m depth range reconfirmed via fresh PADI fetch. CORRECTION: the claim 'ScubaBoard trip reports confirm hammerhead sightings at Contreras-area sites including in September 2024' has been REMOVED — a fresh direct fetch of the cited ScubaBoard thread (654201) shows it was posted January 14, 2025 (not '2026' as the markdown footer previously stated — also corrected) and the author explicitly states hammerheads did NOT appear on that trip ('hammerheads didn't show up'). Hammerhead season: sources conflict significantly (panamadivecenter.com/contreras: March-April; other pages: April-May, April-July; thearkdivers.com: June-November) — this conflict is now stated explicitly in the markdown rather than asserting one window. Humpback whales, dolphins, and toad fish/gorgonian corals added to confirmed PADI species list (previously omitted). All other species and depth claims reconfirmed against fresh fetches of PADI, panamadivecenter.com, and divemasteraustin.com.
